text:
alex: ran an nsys capture on the 1k-step microbatch workload. seeing ~30-90us gaps between H2D memcpy end and kernel launch across multiple CUDA streams. looks like a handshake/deadtime, not pure memcpy cost. anyone seen this after the recent batcher/kernel-selection changes?

joanne: can you upload the .qdrep or a timeline PNG? when host thread gets preempted you see the memcpy finish but kernel dispatch delayed. often shows up as CPU-sched gaps in perf.

alex: uploaded a small snapshot to the infra bucket, link in a sec. quick excerpt from timeline:
```
stream 3: memcpy H2D [0.00ms - 0.14ms] 
stream 3: --- 0.08ms idle ---
stream 3: kernel A [0.22ms - 0.95ms]
```
gaps line up with host callback/handshake region, not GPU busy.

siva: two guesses: 1) kernel splay from the new kernel-selection heuristics — we allow more concurrent kernels which can change stream ordering and copy-engine queuing, 2) batching changed the timing so many H2D requests hit the copy engine back-to-back causing serialization. can you filter nsight for "Memcpy" and the copy-engine lane?

ben: also saw KV cache churn cause the same symptom — prefetch-miss triggers extra page copies on the same stream and kernels have to wait. check logs for "kvcache: page_copy" markers. if kvcache eviction frequency increased, host will be doing more memcpys and you get visible handoff jitter.

maria: are these runs with the new batching heuristic (v3) and model v2? sequence length distribution or padding changed? higher variance in seq len can increase concurrent hostcopy volume.

infra-bot: CI trace uploaded: https://ci.internal/trace/2897654321 (includes qdrep + timeline PNG + perf sampling tar).

joanne: repro steps I used earlier that show the problem reliably:
```
NSYS_NVTX=1 
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --sample=cpu -o /tmp/handshake.qdrep 
  ./bin/serve --workload=microbatch --steps=1000 --batch-size=8
```
open /tmp/handshake.qdrep in Nsight Systems, enable "Memcpy" and host-thread view, look for ~50-200ms CPU-sched gaps. also run `perf record -g -p <pid>` while reproing to catch preemptions.

alex: ran that with `--sample=cpu-sched` and attached link. initial glance: memcpy tails and kernel launch gaps correlate with small but consistent CPU-sched slices where the host thread is off-CPU ~50-120us. interestingly, happens only when serving two model instances concurrently on the same node. single-model runs don't show it.

siva: action items to isolate: 1) repro with CPU affinity (taskset) to rule out OS preemption 2) try `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to confirm scheduling-only vs driver reordering 3) test `batcher.max_concurrent_kernels=2` (down from 4) to see if reducing parallel kernels removes splay.

ben: i'll also enable extra kvcache telemetry (prefetch hits/misses + page_copy counts) and run the same trace. if KV churn is the root cause we'll see spikes aligned with the memcpy bursts.

maria: good. if CPU preemption is the immediate cause we should consider pinning the host worker threads to isolated cores in Dedicated. otherwise we might need to change the batching heuristic to stagger prefetches.

joanne: small perf tip: in Nsight use the "CUDA Streams" view and hide idle lanes, then right-click a memcpy and select "Show related CPU range" — it'll jump to the host thread NVTX/stack. that quickly shows whether it's host scheduling or driver latency. also inspect the copy-engine queue depth column.

alex: assigning owners: alex -> collect full traces & taskset experiments, ben -> kvcache logs & telemetry, joanne -> perf samples and Nsight screenshots. sync in 2 hours?

maria: i'm in for the sync. add results to the infra trace ticket: TICKET-1428.

ben: will try the kvcache patch now, ping when done. :thumbsup:

alex: uploaded compressed qdrep + perf tar to the ticket. thanks folks, will post results from taskset run in the sync.
